definition: SIP refers to social information processing skills, meaning the mental abilities children use to take in and work through social information. In this source, stronger SIP skills are described as a target of social skills training and are linked with better cognitive concentration.

reasons: The packet does not define SIP as “social information processing skills” involving “mental abilities…to take in and work through social information.” It only refers to “children’s SIP skills” as something that can be “enhancing” in social skills training.

While the packet supports that social skills training focused on enhancing children’s SIP skills is linked to “augmenting their cognitive concentration,” it does not clearly support the additional wording that “stronger SIP skills are described as a target of social skills training” (it says training is focused on enhancing SIP skills, but the definition’s specific phrasing is not fully evidenced. )

The expansion of SIP as children’s ‘mental abilities ... to take in and work through social information’ is not stated in the packet and goes beyond the supplied wording ‘social information processing skills.’
‘Stronger’ SIP skills is an unsupported embellishment; the source only says that enhancing children’s SIP skills is an effective strategy for augmenting cognitive concentration.
